summary: This Wikipedia article describes Arizona, a state in the southwestern United States that is part of the Western and Mountain states. It covers the state's size and population ranking, its capital and largest city Phoenix, its neighboring states and Mexican neighbors, and an infobox of official facts such as nicknames, motto, languages, governance, time zones and admission to the Union on February 14, 1912.
one_line: Overview of Arizona, a sixth-largest, 14th-most-populous southwestern U.S. state with capital Phoenix, admitted to the Union in 1912.
key_facts: Arizona is a state in the southwestern region of the United States and is part of the Western and Mountain states.
Arizona is the sixth largest and the 14th most populous of the 50 states.
The capital and largest city of Arizona is Phoenix.
Arizona shares the Four Corners region with Utah, Colorado, and New Mexico.
Arizona's other neighboring states are Nevada and California to the west.
Arizona borders the Mexican states of Sonora and Baja California to the south and southwest.
Arizona's nicknames are The Grand Canyon State and The Copper State.
Arizona's motto is Ditat Deus (God enriches).
Arizona was admitted to the Union on February 14, 1912, as the 48th state.
As of 2010, English was spoken by 74.1% of Arizonans and Spanish by 19.5%.
Arizona's total area is 113,990 sq mi (295,234 km), and it is 0.35% water.
The 2016 estimated population of Arizona was 6,931,071, with a density of 57 per sq mi.
Humphreys Peak, at 12,637 ft (3852 m), is the highest point in Arizona.
The lowest point is the Colorado River at the Sonora border, at 72 ft (22 m).
Arizona's U.S. Senators in the note are John McCain (R) and Jeff Flake (R), and its governor is Doug Ducey (R).
